newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end little changed.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end little changed.

text.p: Swiss shares ended a volatile day virtually unchanged while investors concentrated on banking group Swiss Bank Corp (SBC).

SBC added 4.75 francs, or 2.01 percent, to end at 241.50 after announcing a restructuring of its domestic operations. The measures include 1,700 job cuts, write-offs totalling 3.3 billion francs. SBC also forecast of a 1996 loss of 1.9 billion francs.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index closed 0.1 points higher at 3,690.1. The all-share Swiss Performance Index lost 1.25 points, or 0.05 percent, to end at 2,365.47.
Other banks, expected by the market to take similar measures, followed SBC's footsteps. UBS bearer shares were up 16 francs to 1,160. CS Holding gained 1.25 francs to end at 123.75.
Zurich Insurance rose two francs to 332. After the market closed Zurich reported a 32.7 percent rise in its first half net profit.
Elektrowatt jumped 2.8 percent to 512 francs. One trader said there were rumours in the market that CS Holding was set to divest its stake of around 45 percent in Elektrowatt.
But a CS Holding spokesman said the group had a policy of not commenting on market rumours.
Roche certificates were five francs higher at 9,265 while other pharmaceuticals were generally lower.
